speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As a small island nation, we needed a safe and reliable supply of water to ensure our survival and prosperity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Through decades of long-term planning, innovation and investments, we have built up our Four National Taps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Behind each tap lies an integrated water system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This comprises 17 reservoirs and water catchment covering two-thirds of Singapore's total land area, 15 water treatment plants, four water reclamation plants and an island-wide network of water pipelines, drainage and sewerage systems, and the list goes on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We have overcomed droughts and floods and cleaned up our rivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: And we now enjoy a world-class water system producing safe and reliable drinking water at the turn of the tap, anytime and anywhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It is increasingly challenging for Singapore to ensure water security and meet the water needs of our growing population and economy due to two factors: one, climate change; and two, increased water demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Some of us may recall that we experienced prolonged dry conditions from around 2014 to 2016, when we last experienced a major El Niño event.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: At that time, we saw water levels in the Linggiu Reservoir in Johor plunge to an historic low of 20%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This was a far cry from healthy reservoir levels of 80%-90% which we were used to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This was very worrying because the depletion of the Linggiu Reservoir would affect our supply of imported water from Malaysia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It took five years for the reservoir to reach healthy levels again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Likewise, water levels in local waterbodies also fell during the prolonged dry conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This demonstrates the importance of long-term planning and investment in weather-resilient water sources like NEWater and desalination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Unfortunately, we cannot prevent a recurrence of such extreme weather events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In fact, climate change is likely to cause such extreme weather events to occur more frequently and with more severe impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: According to recent reports by the United Nation's World Meteorological Organisation, global temperatures will likely surge to record levels over the next five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This year, the naturally occurring El Niño is underway once again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will further raise global temperatures and aggravate the risk of prolonged drought, adding additional stress to our water supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The temperatures we have experienced here in Singapore for the past couple of weeks, also speak to this increasing trend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The experience of the previous major El Niño event is a stark reminder that we must not be complacent about our water security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Second, we also need to expect an increase in demand for resources like water, as our population and economy grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is especially so as we continue to draw in and grow high-value but water-intensive industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This includes the wafer fabrication, biomedical and electronic industries, as engines of economic growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It is neither sustainable nor practical in land-scarce Singapore to rely only on building more and more water infrastructure to meet our ever-increasing water needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Besides competing for land with other uses, construction costs have also risen significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is especially so as we need to construct more of our water infrastructure underground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Each new drop of water costs more than the last.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Our newer water sources like NEWater and desalinated water, are energy-intensive and costly to produce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These factors will add pressure for the Government to increase the water price to fund and operate such infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Hence, it is crucial that we carefully manage the growth in our water demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Sustainable growth in water demand allows us to build additional water infrastructure at a more measured pace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This contributes to a more sustainable cost of producing and supplying water in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will also introduce amendments related to the Public Utilities Board (PUB)'s operations, to better support their efforts in ensuring the security of our water supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: I will elaborate on each group of these amendments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Currently, water demand from the non-domestic sector accounts for about half of our total water consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will increase to about two-thirds of our total water demand by 2065.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We must, therefore, make greater efforts to achieve a more sustainable growth in non-domestic water demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: An important strategy is to raise water efficiency, particularly for large water users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: During the Committee of Supply (COS) earlier this year, my Ministry announced that we will be introducing mandatory recycling requirements on new projects in the wafer fabrication, electronics and biomedical industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Clause 12 of the Bill will insert a new section 40 in the PUA to reflect this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: I will now elaborate on how we arrived at the specific requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We considered two key factors in determining which industries to introduce water efficiency requirements for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: First, extent of water demand; and secondly, potential for water recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The largest water consumers are companies in the wafer fabrication, biomedical and electronics industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: They require large amounts of water for their manufacturing processes, such as rinsing and cooling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Collectively, these companies take up almost one-fifth of the total non-domestic water demand today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: And given the strong investment interest which Singapore has attracted from semiconductor and biotechnological firms in recent years, the projected water demand from the non-domestic sector is expected to increase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We are keen to work with companies in these industries to conserve and improve water efficiency, and thus reduce the growth in water demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Apart from looking at industries with high water demand, we also shortlisted those with processes that have high potential for water recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This refers to processes that produce fairly clean used or reject water streams, and thus easier to recycle as minimal treatment is required.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This allows for water recycling to be done cost effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With business costs and competitiveness in mind, we want to ensure that any requirements imposed will be economically and technologically feasible and viable for the companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The wafer fabrication, electronics and biomedical industries fulfil both these criteria of having high water demand and producing water streams with high potential for recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: However, we also recognise that they each use water differently, and processes can differ from one facility to another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: So, we will apply targeted water efficiency requirements specific to the context of these industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We have observed that current technologies already allow companies to achieve such high recycling rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For example, the majority of wafer fabrication plants in Taiwan have achieved a recycling rate of at least 75%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In consultation with the industry and recognising Singapore's unique land constraints, we determined that, for a start, a 50% recycling rate will strike an appropriate balance between having a higher recycling rate, and the technological and economic viability of doing so from the companies' perspective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will review the effectiveness and the impact of the proposed requirements, alongside future changes in technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For the electronics and biomedical industries, processes are much more diverse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This includes reject streams from processes, such as microfiltration, ultrafiltration and reverse osmosis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: They have implemented projects to recycle their reject streams and recover effluents from wastewater.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These requirements will not be applied to existing projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We are focusing on new projects as waste stream segregation for water recycling can be designed upfront.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Beyond designing for recycling, occupiers of the new projects will also be responsible for ensuring that recycling is done while these projects are in operation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Existing projects will not be subjected to the new requirements as they will likely face space limitations when recycling equipment had not been planned for previously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Nonetheless, PUB will continue to work with companies which are keen to increase the recycling rates in existing plants through facilitative measures, such as funding and technical support for recycling projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: PUB and Economic Development Board have engaged affected companies and industry associations in 2021 and 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: They were generally supportive of the proposed requirements and agreed with the technical and economic viability of these requirements for new projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is also in line with the stated sustainability or environmental goals of many of these companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Companies can recover the cost of their investments over time and enjoy cost savings in the longer term through reduced water usage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Some companies have even expressed interest in raising their water recycling rates for new projects beyond the mandated 50% and asked if the Government would support their efforts in doing so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will provide financial support for companies that are willing to invest in technologies to raise their water recycling rate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: PUB reviewed its funding framework for the Water Efficiency Fund (WEF) and the Industrial Water Solution Demonstration Fund (IWSDF), which provide financial support for companies with projects on water recycling and adoption of water-efficient equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We understand that some companies may require additional time and support to adjust to the new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Thereafter, WEF funding will only be eligible for companies looking to raise their recycling rates above the mandatory requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The enhanced funding incentives will make it more economically viable for the companies to introduce larger-scale water recycling projects, as it greatly reduces their payback period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is especially so amongst those who recycle above the mandated 50%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Take GlobalFoundries, for example, a wafer fabrication manufacturing company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Its water recycling project will use innovative state-of-the-art technologies to treat and recycle wastewater from their manufacturing processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With funding support from PUB’s IWSDF for their new project, GlobalFoundries will be able to raise their recycling rates by 10 percentage points, from 45% to 55%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: I am glad that companies, such as GlobalFoundries, are actively embracing water recycling as part of their sustainability goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Besides funding support, PUB provides technical advice on design plans for new facilities and operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: PUB stands ready to support the industries’ initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will improve the industries’ competitiveness and strengthen Singapore’s overall water resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Besides managing water demand by introducing water efficiency requirements, ensuring a stable water supply is equally important for our water security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The next group of amendments introduces charges to large private water suppliers (PWS) to ensure sustainable growth in Singapore’s private water supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: PWS refers to entities other than PUB that harvest rainwater or desalinate seawater following PUB’s approval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Currently, we have a small private water supply sector that supplies about 1% of the total water demand in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The sector comprises private desalination plants and rainwater harvesters of various sizes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In recent years, PUB has received an increased number of proposals from PWS to collect rainwater or extract and treat seawater, to provide non-potable water for their own use or for sale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The number of large rainwater harvesters has tripled since 2013 and we expect interest to continue rising.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We recognise that in the water supply landscape, PWS provides water that is fit-for-purpose, which allows for the more efficient use of water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Nonetheless, to ensure overall water resilience, PUB is still expected to maintain sufficient reserve capacity and be ready to ramp up water production at short notice to make up for any disruptions that are faced by PWS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For instance, in a prolonged drought scenario, large rain harvesters will turn to PUB-supplied water sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Furthermore, PUB must develop and maintain sufficient capacity in our sewer network and water reclamation plants to collect and treat used water from PWS and their customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: So, on this basis, the same principles of water conservation and the same contribution towards the national used water system should apply to PWS, just like how they apply to all other water users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We need to ensure that the growth of the private supply of water remains sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These two principles are reflected in the pricing of PUB-supplied water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Besides water tariffs, PUB’s customers are subjected to the waterborne tax (WBT) and the water conservation tax (WCT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The WBT is a tax contribution to the national used water system paid by all water users, regardless of whether the premises are connected to PUB’s used water network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The WCT is a tax to encourage water conservation and to reflect the scarcity value of water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Today, PWS’ customers do not pay the WCT nor the WBT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Clauses 4 and 5 of the Bill introduce amendments to align the treatment of privately supplied water with the existing charging principles for PUB-supplied water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Clause 5 of the Bill will insert a new section 20A to enable the WCT to be imposed under the PUA instead of the Statutory Board (Taxable Services) Act 1968.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The new section 20A will also allow for the scope of the WCT to be expanded to cover water supplied by PWS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will take a practical and calibrated approach and impose these charges only on large PWS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To be clear, smaller-scale rainwater harvesters, such as those in some housing estates or households, will not be affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is equivalent to around 26,000 typical water pails that are commonly used in households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This threshold was determined based on the average daily usage of water by larger rainwater harvesters who collectively harvest the majority of the volume of all privately harvested water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The WBT will be applied to the volume of water supplied for both their own use and for sale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is in line with the principle of WBT as a tax contribution to the national used water system paid by all water users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The WCT will only be imposed on water supplied for sale by private desalination plants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The WCT will not be applied to desalination plants supplying water for their own use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is because we recognise that there is already a strong business motivation to conserve water due to the high cost of desalination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It will also not apply to rainwater harvesters since they are already helping to conserve treated water by using rainwater.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Small-scale rainwater harvesters with smaller tank sizes of 350 cubic metres and below will not be affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: And those not affected will include those in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates, community clubs, schools and commercial entities with tank sizes that do not exceed the threshold I just mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: PUB will be installing water meters at the PWS’ premises to measure the volume of water supplied for own use or for sale by these large PWS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will allow PUB to obtain accurate readings of the volume of water used or supplied by the PWS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Clause 6 of the Bill will amend section 24A to empower PUB to carry out the water meter installation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The amendments to section 24A will also empower PUB to require the owner or occupier of the premises to carry out works at the premises that are necessary for the installation of the water meter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We appreciate that the charges will add to PWS’ operating costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: PUB has engaged the affected PWS on the new pricing policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The comments and queries received from the rainwater harvesters thus far had been clarificatory in nature, such as how water use would be metered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Owners of private desalination plants raised concerns on the increase in operating costs, especially given the poor business outlook.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These amendments serve to ensure that the Act remains relevant and effective in empowering PUB to carry out its work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: First, clause 7 relates to powers for PUB to recover the cost of removing the obstruction during emergencies where PUB must act immediately, such as removing obstruction to fix pipe bursts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Clause 10 introduces amendments to broaden PUB’s powers to require relevant persons to remove obstructions over all components of the water installation for repair and maintenance works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Second, clause 8 introduces requirements for developers to submit diversion plans for PUB’s approval before they start relocating PUB’s water installations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is to prevent disruptions to water supply and to ensure that the relocated water installations meet PUB’s standards and requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The relocation of such installations without PUB’s approval will be an offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Third, clauses 4 and 5 deal with matters related to the components of water price reflected in water bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The WCT provisions will be moved from the Statutory Board Taxable Services Act 1968 to the PUA, as mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will bring all water price-related provisions under the PUA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: PUB will be empowered to grant, with the Minister’s approval, rebates or waivers on components of the water bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This power may be exercised to grant "leak concessions", for instance, where water is lost through a leak that is beyond a customer’s control and the circumstances justify a reduction in the amount of the water bill to account for the leak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This provides a transition period so that customers have sufficient time to seek redress before the time-bar comes into effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This brings us in line with the overall Government policy to promote digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will also introduce related amendments to the Sewerage and Drainage Act (SDA) under clause 20 to similarly update the service requirements for the purpose of SDA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In summary, Sir, there is a strong impetus for us to manage growth in water demand and ensure a resilient water supply for Singapore, in order to meet the long-term needs of our economy and our population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The proposed amendments to PUA will provide PUB with the legislative powers to do so and incentivise industries to do even more to conserve and recycle water through introducing water efficiency requirements to water-intensive industries, and charges on large PWS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The proposed amendments related to PUB’s operations will allow PUB to more effectively and efficiently fulfil its mission of safeguarding our water security and continue to ensure a safe and reliable water supply for all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It lists situations where a different WBT can be imposed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The explanatory statement states that this amendment is to allow finer calibration to the circumstances where WBT is imposed and the amount of WBT imposed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share specifically what changes to the imposition and calibration of WBT are envisaged?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also share if the list is intended to be exhaustive?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the list is not exhaustive, will PUB make clear the basis for imposing differentiated WBT?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on PUB's power on the relocation of any water installation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 26 sets out PUB's powers on the water installations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If so, how will the quantum of payment be determined?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, section 26(10) allows an authorised officer to enter the premises and carry out works or take any measures if a person fails to comply with a notice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given the intrusiveness of these powers, can the Senior Minister of State confirm that reasonable time will be given for a person to comply with the notice?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also confirm that force cannot be used to secure any entry?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What are the types of other measures that an authorised officer may take if there is non-compliance?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My final point is on water efficiency requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 40 of the amendments introduces water efficiency requirements for new facilities built for business purposes that require water.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that there are presently existing best practice guidelines published for certain industries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if further changes will be made to the current best practices guidelines for these industries?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will guidelines be introduced for more industries as well?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also share whether the water efficiency requirements take into account the present technology that is available to maintain water efficiency?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The issue of water supply was a point of tension in bilateral relations between Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There have been occasional disputes and disagreements over water pricing and other related matters.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As water is a critical resource, any change or threat to water supply can have significant implications for Singapore's water security and Independence.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is timely that we discuss this Bill as we celebrate Singapore's 58th birthday next week.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I support this Bill but I have a few points for clarification.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We are competing with many countries like South Korea to attract MNCs in the wafer fabrication, biomedical and electronics industries to set up plants in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will the new water efficiency requirements result in additional cost burdens for these multinational corporations (MNCs)?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This may impact Singapore's competitiveness in attracting companies in these sectors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is the Government doing to support them?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Regarding companies that have genuine reasons for not being able to meet the water efficiency requirements, I hope PUB can take a balanced approach.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While we encourage compliance with water efficiency standards, I hope PUB can also consider the challenges faced by individual companies.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope there will be avenues for companies to seek waivers or apply for exemptions if they can demonstrate valid reasons for not meeting the requirements.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: PUB should assess each case on its merits and decide whether to grant leniency based on the company's circumstances.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Taiwan can achieve a water recycling rate of 75% in the wafer fabrication industry as manufacturers adopt advanced water recycling and treatment technologies.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Government support the development of this technology and upskill the local corporates which play a critical role in this space like advanced water treatment, chemical and particle removal and dilute chemical recovery?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How is the Government addressing this impact in the long run?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What role does PWS play in Singapore's water security strategy and what is the desired PWS landscape in the long term?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Under what type of circumstances will PUB take immediate action to remove obstruction?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Yet, the global challenges of climate change and increasing water demand continue to pose pressing concerns for nations worldwide.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As a country known for our prudent water management in the face of resource constraints, we are particularly vulnerable to these challenges.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As we grapple with the anticipated repercussions of climate change on our water resources, it becomes imperative that we adopt a forward-thinking approach and proactively address these issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, I would like to ask about the mandatory recycling requirements outlined in the proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to expand the mandatory recycling requirements to cover other sectors as well?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can this be stretched to either the financial and business sectors or other manufacturing sectors like pharmaceuticals?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Additionally, it would be beneficial to understand how the Government intends to support these efforts, be it through the provision of infrastructure or subsidies.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I also wish to better understand the difference between the WEF and the IWSDF.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are the funding caps for these initiatives sufficient to make a substantial impact in achieving our water sustainability goals?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Whilst we seek to meet our water recycling goals, we must be mindful of the costs associated with meeting these requirements, in particular, whether having compulsory water recycling would drive up costs of production and make businesses in Singapore less competitive.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I would like to seek clarifications on the introduced charges for PWS.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is their impact on the country's overall water system, particularly in terms of capacity and supply?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How does PUB plan to make sure that by allowing more PWS, we ensure that it does not go the way of the open electricity market, where a number of smaller companies could not sustain their operations and customers were affected?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, I would like to comment on the amendments related to operations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Regarding the provision of legal powers to PUB to conduct operations to safeguard water security, may I ask how often these powers of entry were exercised in the past?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I understand that these powers are essential for maintaining water security, but some may view them as intrusive.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Hence, I seek an explanation on whether the decision to exercise these powers is based on the severity of the issue at hand, ensuring that the entry is justified and proportionate to the situation, something which Member Louis Ng has also mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In addition, I note the decision to give PUB's e-notices to accounts pre-designated by customers the same legal effect as PUB's hard copy documents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I welcome the move towards e-notices as more people are adopting them over paper notices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is also a more efficient and eco-friendly approach.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, I would like to express a concern for some residents, especially seniors, who may have difficulties accessing and reading digital notices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They may have an online account or app, often created on their behalf, but that does not necessarily mean they will use it.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I urge the authorities to ensure that appropriate provisions are in place to accommodate and support residents who may need alternative ways of communication to stay updated on water-related matters.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This could include an opt-out option for those who prefer hard copy notices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These changes align with the urgent need to enhance our water management practices and further enhance the foundation for a sustainable water future.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is reassuring to witness our commitment to the principles of reuse and recycle embedded within this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, it is critical to acknowledge that the journey towards water sustainability extends beyond the measures outlined in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While the focus on reuse and recycle is commendable, we must not overlook the importance of the "reduce" component in our water story.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As a nation with limited natural resources, Singapore must continue to prioritise and persist in public education initiatives that promote water conservation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By instilling a culture of responsible water usage and emphasising the significance of reducing our overall water consumption, we can further safeguard and strengthen our precious water resources.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, as we introduce these initiatives to conserve water, we must ensure that the consumers are not burdened by the costs.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As for the amendments to impose charges on PWS, I have some queries.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: PWS' constructions to collect rainwater or get water from the sea to produce desalinated water need to be approved by PUB.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They complement PUB in providing complementary water supplies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry share the profiles of these PWS?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many are there and have their numbers been increasing in recent years?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many of these are rainwater harvesters and desalination plants?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To whom do they supply their processed waters?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to know if the Ministry had engaged with PWS regarding the proposed measures and discussed their concerns.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What do both parties think would be the likely impact of the new taxes on this sector?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry explain the reasons for the different tax treatments?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, why are all PWS which produce water for their own use exempted from WCT, likewise for rainwater harvesters?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are the private producers inter-company and intra-company, that is, so-called related company sales exempted from WBT and WCT respectively for those within the production compound or a related company at other locations?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I will begin by addressing the issues related to the mandatory water efficiency requirements.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked whether there are plans to mandate a higher recycling rate in the wafer fabrication industry, especially when Taiwan has already achieved a recycling rate of 75%.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip and Mr Don Wee also asked whether the costs associated with meeting the mandatory water recycling requirements will affect the competitiveness of businesses in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I want to thank the Members for these questions, which reflect the importance of striking a balance between ensuring water sustainability and business competitiveness.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As mentioned in my speech earlier, setting the mandatory recycling rate for the wafer fabrication industry requires careful calibration.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We need to strike an appropriate balance between having a higher recycling rate and the technological and economic viability of doing so.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Too low a mandatory recycling rate means that we do not maximise the opportunity to achieve a more sustainable water demand growth.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Too high a recycling rate may be economically prohibitive for several companies, which will end up eroding Singapore's competitiveness.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are mindful of potentially higher operational costs and land constraints that become especially salient when the recycling rate goes beyond 50%, as companies will have to adopt more advanced water treatment technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Also, to address Mr Louis Ng's query on whether existing technology was taken into account when deciding the water efficiency requirements, the Government has taken into account not just technical viability, but also economic viability.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Companies we engaged with agreed that a minimum recycling rate of 50% was technically and economically viable for them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is corroborated by the high recycling rates that the companies have declared for their recently commissioned and upcoming wafer fabrication plants in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In fact, some companies indicated that they aspired to recycle beyond the mandatory level as part of their corporate social responsibility to conserve resources.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: PUB certainly welcomes and supports the aspirations of these companies to achieve higher recycling rates beyond the mandated levels.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As climate action gains greater traction globally and resource sustainability becomes more pertinent, we see that consumers and investors are paying greater attention to corporate sustainability efforts.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is, therefore, in the companies' long-term interests to show their commitment towards water sustainability efforts.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Likewise, it is critical for Singapore to continue to show our commitment to water sustainability as a responsible steward of the environment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Introducing mandatory water recycling requirements is a key part of this effort.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And as Mr Don Wee rightly pointed out, we must remain an attractive investment and business destination.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: He raised an important point on providing support to affected companies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the Water Efficiency Fund (WEF) and the Industrial Water Solutions Demonstration Fund (IWSDF), and whether the funding support is sufficient to make a substantial impact on achieving our water sustainability goals.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Since 2007, PUB has been providing funding support, in addition to technical support, to companies that are looking to invest in technologies to raise their water recycling rates.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: PUB's funding support has greatly reduced companies' payback periods and incentivise them to adopt water-efficient practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Under the WEF, companies may apply for funding to perform water efficiency assessments, implement pilot and full-scale water recycling projects or adopt water-efficient equipment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The IWSDF is a sub-scheme under the WEF and supports the adoption of new technologies and innovative water recycling solutions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The projects should utilise emerging or recently developed technologies or innovative applications of existing technologies which have not been implemented in the industry.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Addressing Mr Don Wee's query on the Government's support for companies affected by the water recycling requirements, the IWSDF allows PUB to co-share with companies the risks of adopting novel water efficiency solutions and, through this, tip the cost-benefit balance in the favour of the companies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Don Wee asked about the Government's support to develop technologies for higher recycling rates and to upskill local businesses in this area.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: PUB, in fact, fosters industry growth through collaborations with local and overseas partners in the water and water-related industries.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Areas of collaboration include research, technology development and knowledge management.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, PUB offers industrial test-bedding sites to help develop new technologies in the water market.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I strongly encourage companies to tap on PUB's support schemes to boost their water recycling efforts.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will review the effectiveness of the proposed requirements, alongside future changes in technology, before considering whether to mandate higher recycling rates or to expand the requirements to other sectors, as Mr Yip has asked.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Importantly, we need to consider that other sectors may have a lower recycling potential due to the heterogenous nature of their processes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is because they may have waste streams that are of a different nature in terms of quality, quantity and content, making it much more challenging and much costlier to recycle water.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Hence, it may not be viable to apply a single mandatory requirement across all industrial sectors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Working with companies and individual sectors to identify relevant water conservation opportunities would be a much more effective approach.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Nonetheless, we may consider extending the requirements in future if it becomes economically and technologically feasible to do so.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the meantime, I encourage businesses in other sectors, such as refineries, petrochemicals and chemicals companies, to refer to PUB's guidelines on best practices to improve water efficiency, as Mr Louis Ng mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether these guidelines would be updated for the wafer fabrication, electronics and biomedical industries in view of the new requirements.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Ng also asked if water efficiency guidelines will be introduced for more industries.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I want to assure Members that the guidelines are reviewed regularly, along with updates to the best practices and case studies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: A second version of the guidebook for wafer fabrication and semiconductor companies was, in fact, published in 2022.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the same year, PUB also introduced three new guidebooks for the commercial laundry, food and beverage manufacturing and biomedical manufacturing companies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Don Wee asked what will happen if companies have genuine reasons for not being able to meet the water efficiency requirements.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: He also asked if waivers can be granted based on valid reasons.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We understand that some companies may face unique challenges in meeting the water efficiency requirements.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Such waivers will be considered on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the specific circumstances of the companies, following PUB's technical assessment of the reasons for waivers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I hope that Members have a better understanding of the importance of managing our water demand growth.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Besides water security, it also ensures that the cost of producing and supplying water remains sustainable for Singapore in the long run.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: By carefully managing water demand growth, we can build our water infrastructure at a more sustainable pace, thereby controlling costs, which Mr Wee had asked about.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I will now move on to address issues related to private water suppliers, or the PWS.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the profiles and number of PWS in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The vast majority are rainwater harvesters, with a small number of private desalination plants.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Most PWS collect rainwater or produce desalinated water for their own use.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Gan and Mr Don Wee asked about our long-term plans for the private water supply sector and the role of PWS in our water supply landscape.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To ensure the resilience of our overall water supply system, we envision a small private water supply sector comprising mostly small-scale PWS, with the bulk of water still supplied by PUB.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The value proposition for PWS is to supply water of varying qualities on a fit-for-purpose basis.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, instead of using potable water, commercial entities harvest rainwater for landscape irrigation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This enhances our overall water security because it encourages the conservation and efficient usage of potable water.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Mr Yip Hon Weng accurately pointed out, PWS or their customers could face water supply disruptions if PWS' operations are affected, or if the PWS ceases supply as a business decision.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Singapore's national water agency, PUB must maintain a sufficient reserve capacity so that we can ramp up water production at short notice to supply to the PWS and/or their customers in the event of disruption in the PWS' operations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Keeping private water supply small would be an important safeguard and manages the enterprise risk for our water system as a whole.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If the PWS sector were to grow multi-fold, the PWS sector would place significantly more risk on our water system, and PUB would then need to provision for and invest in more capacity to ramp up production, in case of any disruptions faced by the PWS or cessation of supply.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: An overly fragmented PWS sector with an excessive number of small operators would also not be able to fully reap economies of scale and be less economically viable and efficient.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh had several clarifications on the charges, including the intent of introducing the charges and how these charges would apply.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I have shared earlier with Members, we want to take a practical and calibrated approach in introducing the charges to PWS.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: When determining the applicable threshold for rainwater harvesters, we considered the overall landscape and profile of rainwater harvesters.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We observed that most PWS are small-scale rainwater harvesters, such as those in HDB estates and schools, which collectively account for around 20% of privately harvested water.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will include entities, such as country clubs, golf courses and industrial premises with tank sizes larger than 350 cubic metres.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked whether the charges would apply to private desalination plants that supply water for their own use within the same premises or to different premises.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have taken a calibrated approach when it comes to the imposition of charges.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, the WBT will apply for private desalination plants for the volume of water supplied, for both their own use and for sale.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is consistent with our approach that all water users contribute to the national used water system.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The WCT is only applicable if the water is supplied to third parties, including subsidiary companies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Gan also asked why the WCT would not be imposed on PWS supplying water for their own use.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The principle behind the WCT is to encourage water conservation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Private desalination plants already have a strong business motivation to conserve water due to the high cost of desalination, while rainwater harvesters are already conserving treated water by just using rainwater.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, imposing WCT on these two types of PWS would, therefore, increase business costs without actually improving water conservation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Gan asked if the charges would discourage PWS from supplying water.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We acknowledge that the charges will add to the PWS' operating costs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: PUB has engaged and will continue to engage the PWS and support them during this transition.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have assessed that, unlike small-scale rainwater harvesters, imposing WBT on large-scale rainwater harvesters is unlikely to discourage them from harvesting rainwater.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is because they benefit from economies of scale that make rainwater a financially viable alternative to PUB-supplied potable water.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Louis Ng pointed out that clause 4 of the Bill allows for the imposition of the WBT to be more finely calibrated and asked what changes to the imposition and calibration of the WBT are envisaged.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To clarify, section 20 currently enables WBT to be charged on water supplied by PUB only.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are amending section 20 to enable WBT to be charged on water supplied by persons other than PUB, namely, the PWS.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Current provisions in section 20 are being expanded to include “extracted water” and “water derived from extracted water”, so that WBT can be calculated with reference to rainwater and desalinated water.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: PUB will make clear the basis for imposing differentiated WBT when such cases arise.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To conclude the segment on PWS, I would like to reiterate that the introduction of charges is aimed at aligning the treatment of privately supplied water with the charging principles for PUB-supplied water.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is to encourage conservation and efficient usage, regardless of its source.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These charges will also help to ensure the sustainable growth of the private water supply sector.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I will now cover the final segment on questions related to PUB’s operations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how often the powers of entry were exercised by PUB in the past and highlighted that such powers should be exercised judiciously and be proportionate to the situation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked whether reasonable advance notice would be provided for compliance with notices and whether force would be used to secure entry to premises.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I believe Mr Yip is referring to clause 6 of the Bill, which amends section 24A of the Act that deals with powers to enter premises for installation or maintenance of pipes, water installations and so on acquired by PUB.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On average, PUB has to request and gain access to private premises eight times a month to carry out such works.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the other hand, Mr Ng is referring to the proposed section 26(10) introduced under clause 8 of the Bill.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The provision allows PUB to enter premises to carry out works or take measures if a person fails to comply with a notice to stop unauthorised relocation of water installations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For both sections, PUB will seek the cooperation of the owners or occupiers and advance notice will be given.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The entry must be at a reasonable hour or otherwise at a time agreed with the owner or occupier of these premises.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The power under section 24A is different from the emergency situations in which PUB has to take immediate action, as Mr Don Wee has asked about.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Under emergency situations, such as a burst in a pipeline running through private property or disruptions to public water supply, PUB must act immediately to remove obstruction or enter private premises without notice to address the urgent and emergency situation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The provision to act in such emergency situations is in section 24B of the Act.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if PUB would make payment to a person who transfers the ownership of a water installation to PUB, as provided in clause 8 of the Bill, which amends section 26 of the Act.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Such diversions are requested solely by the developers carrying out construction works at or in the vicinity of the existing water installation, for their own development projects.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Clause 16 of the Bill amends section 70 of the Act to update the various means by which service of documents may be effected by PUB.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, it will enable PUB to send electronic notices, in place of hard copy documents, to alert customers on high water consumption.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I hope this will give the assurance to the Member who raised the question.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications for Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon?
